title: Displacement field stabilizes even-denominator and partonic fractional quantum Hall states in the $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Landau levels of Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene
authors: Rakesh K. Dora, Udit Khanna, Ajit C. Balram
abstract: Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG), in which a graphene layer is stacked atop another and laterally shifted by a lattice constant, offers remarkable tunability in its single-particle states under applied magnetic and displacement fields. Owing to this tunability, recent transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in the presence of a perpendicular magnetic field and finite interlayer displacement fields have observed even-denominator fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states at half-filling in the first excited, namely, $\mathcal{N}{=}2$, Landau level (LL) of BLG. In contrast, at zero displacement field, a gapless composite fermion Fermi liquid (CFFL) is realized at half-filling of the $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ LL. Motivated by these experiments, we compute the phase diagram as a function of the displacement field in the half-filled $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ LL of BLG by studying the competition between the CFFL and the Moore-Read state---a candidate even-denominator FQH state---by calculating their thermodynamic energies in this setting. We find that the modified effective Coulomb interaction, induced by changes in the single-particle states with increasing displacement field, softens the inter-electronic repulsion at short distances, thereby stabilizing the Moore-Read state over the CFFL in the $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ LL of BLG. We also study the nature of FQH states at fillings $2/5$, $3/7$, $4/9$, and $6/13$ in the $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ LL of BLG. Our results suggest that, with increasing displacement field, the Jain composite-fermion states at $3/7$, $4/9$, and $6/13$ transition into states with distinct topological order that are well-captured by parton wave functions.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how an interlayer displacement field in Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene stabilizes exotic even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states. By comparing the energies of competing correlated states, the authors demonstrate that the displacement field drives the system from a Fermi liquid phase into a topologically ordered Moore-Read state. This work highlights the tunability of correlated electron phases in graphene heterostructures.
main_problem: The study investigates the stabilization of even-denominator and partonic fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states in the N=2 Landau level of Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG). It focuses on the competition between different correlated electronic states.
main_result: Increasing the interlayer displacement field stabilizes the Moore-Read state over the Composite Fermion Fermi Liquid (CFFL) at half-filling. Furthermore, it shows that other FQH states transition into topologically distinct states described by parton wave functions.
method: The authors compute the thermodynamic energies of competing states (like CFFL and Moore-Read) and analyze the phase diagram as a function of the displacement field.
model_or_system: The physical system is Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG) under a perpendicular magnetic field and an interlayer displacement field. The analysis is performed within the context of the N=2 Landau level, treating the electron-electron interaction via effective Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Fractional quantum Hall states at fillings like 1/2, 2/5, 3/7, 4/9, and 6/13; the competition between CFFL and Moore-Read states.
important_parameters:
Interlayer displacement field, perpendicular magnetic field, and specific filling fractions ($
u$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical calculation is performed in the thermodynamic limit, and the study notes that other competing phases (like Wigner crystals) were not fully considered.
figures_summary: The main results are summarized in phase diagrams (e.g., Fig. 9) showing the transition between different electronic phases as a function of the displacement field.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon experimental observations of FQH states in BLG, develops a theoretical framework by calculating the energy competition between candidate states (CFFL vs. MR), and maps out the resulting phase diagram across various fillings.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how external tuning parameters (like displacement fields) can stabilize exotic, topologically ordered correlated states in a tunable solid-state system, which is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory.
